benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: ICE Brent (January contract) rose to about $92.57/bbl on 20 Nov, up 64 cents on the day (Trading Economics), from $91.98 the day before, as Iran's attacks on US-linked bases in Bahrain and new unverified tanker-mine claims near Hormuz offset bearish US inventory data; still down from $95.84 a week earlier (13 Nov).

note: Brent (January contract) rose to about $92.57/bbl on 20 Nov, up from $91.98 the day before but still down from $95.84 a week earlier, while WTI rose to $83.41. Iran launched drone and missile attacks on US-linked bases in Bahrain on 21 Nov, and is staging a 14-tanker convoy at Kharg Island to try to run the US naval blockade, per Iranian media and independent ship-tracking (Windward, UANI); new unverified tanker-mine claims and UKMTO-reported projectile strikes hit shipping near Hormuz the same day. Those gains offset bearish signals from an EIA report showing larger-than-expected US crude and gasoline stock builds for the week to 13 Nov, and from Reuters reporting that Ukrainian drone strikes have cut Russian oil refining by about 45% since late October. TTF rose to about €88.45/MWh on 20 Nov and JKM to $28.42; Henry Hub rose to about $3.41 on colder weather forecasts, still largely insulated from the Gulf and Red Sea turmoil.
